item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Oct 27, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Chills, Thrills and that Spooky Stuff: Horror of the Early '60s with Kevin Stairiker! — Wed Oct 28, 6:15 PM — Manheim Township
item.description:
Discussion, Movie & Film, Adults, Seniors

Styles may change, but a classic jump-scare can still creep out a fresh generation of moviegoers. 🎬This October, test your brave side with us! 🎃 Every Tuesday night starting at 6pm, we’re screening legendary fright flicks that have given movie lovers the wiggles, the willies, and full-blown goosebumps for decades. 🍿 Hosted by Kevin Stairiker (LNP | LancasterOnline), each evening packs in creepy cinema, post-movie chats, light snacks, and maximum eerie vibes. 🕷️ Bring your courage (and a friend to hide behind)! 👀✨October 5th: City of the Dead, 1960, 78 minutesOctober 20th: Black Sabbath, 1963, 93 minutesOctober 28th: The Innocents, 1961, 100 minutesRegistration is encouraged!

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Nov 4, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.

item.title: "Persuasion" - A One Act Play Inspired by Jane Austen — Fri Nov 6, 7:00 PM — Historic Rock Ford
item.description:
“Persuasion” relates the story of Anne Elliot, an aristocratic young lady who declines marrying Captain Frederick Wentworth at a youthful age even though she deeply loves him. After a period of seven years, Anne and Wentworth meet again and must resolve their feelings through a series of encounters that are highlighted in the play. This one-act play, inspired by scenes from Jane Austen’s novel, was adapted for Historic Rock Ford by Samuel Slaymaker. .
Performance Dates: November 6, 7 , 13,14, 21 from 7-8:30 PM ; November 22 from 2-3:30 PM Where: First floor of the Circa 1794 General Hand Mansion.
Due to space constraints within the rooms of the Hand Mansion, audiences are limited to 15 guests per performance. Guests are standing for the entire performance and will be moving from room to room following the action of the play. Tickets must be purchased in advance through ticketing link. Due to limited space for each performance, tickets will not be available at the door

item.title: We the People First Friday: Heartland Marimba Festival — Fri Nov 6, 7:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Make the Ware Center for the Arts part of your Lancaster City First Friday route! Join us in November as Heartland Marimba presents a hands-on, behind-the-scenes look at the marimba, and a new art exhibit opens in the Regitz Gallery.
At 7 pm in the lobby, join the members of Heartland Marimba as they reveal all the insider goodies about their fascinating instrument. Listen, touch, and learn as you explore the science of its acoustics, trace its history from Africa to Central America to the classical music stage, and hear the untold stories of the marimba’s Pennsylvania roots—including tales of the “godfather” of classical marimba, Clair Musser, who hailed from Manheim, PA.
From 5-8 in the Regitz Gallery, explore a new gallery exhibit by Lancaster artist Shauna L. Yorty, “Overshare: I Did This for Me.” Through cardboard collages, mixed media pieces, and bright, bold works of art, Yorty invites viewers to witness vulnerability, embrace their own stories, and find connection to themselv

item.title: “A Pipe Organ Feast” — Fri Nov 6, 8:00 PM — First Reformed Church
item.description:
A veritable feast of pipe organ music will be presented by organist Larry Hershey at First Reformed Church of Lancaster. The free 30 minute concert will include “For All the Saints” by Leo Sowerby, Carlo Curley’s spectacular arrangement of “Largo” from Dvorak’s New World Symphony, and “Variations on ‘Christus Vincit’” by Denis Bedard. The concert will conclude with Virgil Fox’s dazzling arrangement of Bach’s “Now Thank We All Our God.”
The First Friday “Organic Reflections” concert series is a gift to the community from First Reformed Church, a center city congregation of the United Church of Christ. Only 30 minutes in length, the free concerts begin at 8 PM each First Friday for the convenience of those who wish to spend the early evening visiting downtown galleries before the concert. Doors open at 7:30 pm. All are welcome to hear 30 minutes of majestic music that will refresh your soul and inspire your spirit.

item.title: Body Talks — Sat Nov 7, 10:00 AM — Urban Arts House
item.description:
Body Talks is a Saturday morning gathering for women who want to have honest conversations about bodies, confidence, aging, sex, visibility and what it actually feels like to live in a body that is changing. The body you have vs. the body you were told you should have. When did having a body become so much work? The weight. The clothes. The cellulite. The aging. The comparison. The constant feeling that we should be doing something to make our bodies better. And somewhere along the way, a lot of us stopped actually living in our bodies and started managing them instead. So let’s talk about it. And yes, there will be mimosas (N/A option available too!).

item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
